headline: Benchmarks and dosage-aware corrections reshape genomic and epigenomic readout calling
label: Genomic Context In Sequencing Readouts
summary: Assembly, benchmarking, and dosage-aware calling studies show reference-dependent choices bias genomic and epigenomic measurements.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that sequencing-derived readouts depend on reference context, and that internal controls or standardized benchmarks are needed to evaluate them. A telomere-to-telomere human assembly built from HERRO-corrected Nanopore Simplex reads with Verkko2 establishes a complete reference, while TUSCO uses a curated single-isoform gene set as internal ground truth for long-read transcriptome reconstruction. MethylBench compares six DNA methylation technologies on GIAB and blood and fibroblast samples. A preprint shows that local DNA dosage from copy number and replication timing distorts ATAC-seq peak calling, with WGS control proposed as correction and released as open-source MACS-based software. What is new here is the explicit use of WGS-derived dosage control in peak calling. STARCall and rhapsodist address scalability of imaging-based and single-cell processing pipelines rather than this question.
